# Introduction

This Quarto document demonstrates
(1) how DynLib tables can be retrieved in R.
(2) how the DynLib infrastructure interoperates with the R for Mass Spectrometry
    ecosystem.
(3) how to use RDynLib Accessors for Compound and Spectral Data.

# Setup and direct access to DynLib SQL databases
## Load required R packages

```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
library(here)
library(Spectra)
library(CompoundDb)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
#library(RDynLib)
library(devtools)
load_all()
```


## Download and connect to a DynLib SQL database
```{r}
# maize_FTneg
get_dynlib_zenodo(
  doi = ,
  file = "maize_ftmsneg.sqlite",
  destdir = "data"
)
maize_ftneg <- here("data", "maize_ftneg.sqlite")
con_mftneg <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), maize_ftneg)
```

## Retrieve DynLib database tables directly

```{r}
# List available tables in the DynLib SQL database
DBI::dbListTables(con_mftneg)

# Retrieve tables
experiment <- DBI::dbReadTable(con_mftneg, "experiment")
ms_compound <- DBI::dbReadTable(con_mftneg, "experiment")
msms_spectrum <- DBI::dbReadTable(con_mftneg, "experiment")
msms_spectrum_peak <- DBI::dbReadTable(con_mftneg, "experiment")

table(experiment$expid)

```

## Disconnect from the SQL database

Once the required tables have been retrieved, the database connection can be closed using `dbDisconnect()`. The `CompDb` and `Spectra` objects introduced in the following section can be created directly from the database file path.

```{r}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con_mftneg)
```

# Accessing DynLib data through R for Mass Spectrometry
Both `CompDb` and `Spectra` objects provide access to the R for Mass Spectrometry ecosystem. While `CompDb` offers a database-centric interface for querying and managing compound database content,`Spectra` provides a more spectrum-centric interface.

## Working with CompDb objects

### Creating a CompDb object from a DynLib database
We create a `CompDb` object `cdb` from the DynLib SQL database using the `ExpCompDb()` function from the `RDynLib` package. The resulting `CompDb` object represents the complete SQL database and provides access to all of its tables.
```{r}
cdb <- ExpCompDb(maize_ftneg)
# Print database metadada information
meta <- metadata(cdb)
head(meta)
str(cdb)
```

### Retrieving and filtering compound information
Compound information can be extracted from a `CompDb` object using the `compounds()` function from the `CompoundDb` package. The resulting table corresponds to the `ms_compound` table in the SQL database and contains the compound identifier (compound_id), together with chromatographic information such as m/z and retention time, and structural annotation data, such as the compound name and molecular formula. By applying filters in the `compounds()` function, one can create a subsetted ms_compund table with compound identifiers (compound_id) of selected compounds corresponding to a defined value for `name` or `exactmass`.



The compound information of specific criteria:
```{r}
supportedFilters(cdb)
compounds(cdb, columns = c("compound_id", "name", "formula", "expid"))

```

```{r}
compounds(cdb, columns = c("compound_id", "name", "formula", "expid"),
          filter = ~ name == "maysin 2 PU KM")
```

For more queries and details visit this workflow: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages//release/bioc/vignettes/CompoundDb/inst/doc/CompoundDb-usage.html

These filters require prior knowledge of the compound name or theoretical exact mass and are therefore not suitable for retrieving uncharacterized compounds based on their experimental m/z or retention time. For this purpose, RDynLib provides dedicated accessor functions (see the section "RDynLib accessors for retrieving compound and spectral data" below).

## Working with Spectra objects

### Creating a Spectra object from a DynLib database
A `CompDb` object can be converted into a `Spectra` object using the `Spectra()` function from the `Spectra` package. By default, the MzBackendCompDb backend is used, which keeps the spectra linked to the underlying compound database, allowing the entire database to be accessed through the resulting `Spectra` object.
Alternatively, `RDynLib` provides a function to convert a DynLib SQL database directly into a Spectra object with MzBackendCompDb backend. 

```{r}
# Using the Spectra package:
sps <- Spectra(cdb)
sps

# Using the RDynLib package:
sps.rdl <- sql_to_spectra(sql_db)

str(sps)
str(sps.rdl)
```
The objects `sps` and `sps.rdl` are exactly the same `Spectra` objects.

### Accessing spectral metadata

Print spectra variables:
```{r}
spectraVariables(sps)
```

Print spectra Data:
```{r}
spectraData(sps, columns = c("msLevel" , "retention_time", "precursorMz",
                                "centroided","scanIndex", "dataOrigin", 
                                "compound_id", "nodename" 
                                ))
```

All the columns from the original SQL table are preserved and reported in 
the spectraData of the `Spectra` object.

# RDynLib Accessors for retrieving compound and spectral data
DynLib is designed to store information on both characterized and uncharacterized compounds. RDynLib provides dedicated accessor functions, to complement the functionality of `CompoundDb` and `Spectra`, allowing to retrieve compound and spectral information for uncharacterized compounds, even when exact theoretical mass or the compound name are unknown. These functions allow users to search for compounds based on experimental properties or available annotations (`filterCompounds()`), or to retrieve compound information (`get_compound()`), and spectral metadata (`get_spectrum_id()`) based on `compound_id`.


## Filtering compounds by experimental properties and annotation
RDynLib provides `filterCompounds()` to retrieve compound records based on experimental properties and available annotations. The `filterCompounds()` function allows filtering by measured m/z, retention time, nodename, complete or partial compound name, and experiment identifier. Multiple filtering criteria can be combined.

Retrieve compounds in experiment 191 with a measured m/z between 537.1 and 537.3:

```{r}
filterCompounds(
  sql_path = maize_ftneg,
  expid = 191,
  mass_measured = 537.2,
  mass_tolerance = 0.1
)

```

Retrieve compounds, in all experiments of the maize ftneg DynLib database, whose name contains "DIMBOA":

```{r}
filterCompounds(maize_ftneg, name = "DIMBOA")
```


Multiple filtering criteria can be combined, for example to retrieve compounds within specified m/z and retention time windows:

```{r}
filterCompounds(
  maize_ftneg,
  expid = 192,
  name = "DIMBOA",
  mass_measured = 372,
  mass_tolerance = 0.5,
  retention_time = 10,
  rt_tolerance = 2
)
```

## Retrieve compound information by compound ID
RDynLib provides `get_compound()` to retrieve the `ms_compound` table of a given `compound_id`.
```{r}
compound <- get_compound(qt_path = maize_ftneg, compound_id = 63846)
compound
```

## Retrieve spectral information by compound ID
RDynLib provides `get_spectrum_id()` to retrieve spectrum identifiers (`spectrum_id`) and spectral metadata, associated to a compound_id, for subsequent extraction of MS/MS or MS$^n$ spectra. 

Show the msms_spectrum table of a given compound_id
```{r}
sp_id <- get_spectrum_id(qt_path = maize_ftneg, compound_id = 63846 )
sp_id
```

Retrieve the corresponding spectrum using `filterValues()` from the `Spectra` package:

```{r}
sp <- sql_to_spectra(maize_ftneg)
sp_selected <- filterValues(sp, "spectrum_id", sp_id$spectrum_id)
```

Display the m/z and intensity values of the spectrum:

```{r}
peaksData(sp_selected)[[1]]
```

```{r}
MSnplot_SQL(maize_ftneg, 63846, thr_int = 10)
```
